description: Design, execute, and monitor multi-step task flows — create flows through conversation or the visual canvas; execute them with live node-by-node animation

tool_definition.name: TDA_Flow
tool_definition.description: Manages task flows. Call when user wants to create, design, edit, execute, or inspect a workflow of connected tasks. Flows can include LLM tasks, function tasks, decision branches, judges, canvas artefacts, and loops over task segments.

flow_id.description: Flow ID. Required for all actions except 'create' and 'list'.

node.description: Node definition for 'add_node'. Fields: id (optional, auto-generated), type ('task_llm'|'task_tool'|'task_prompt'|'task_function'|'decision'|'merge'|'start'|'end'[[gate:files]]|'file_input'|'file_output'[[/gate]]), label, data, position ({x,y}). data by type: task_llm {prompt, profile_id}; task_tool {tool_name, arguments}; [[gate:act]]task_action {action, invocation:{key, values}, profile_id} (a SIGNED action the agent performs unattended — its posture decides; the agent must be granted the action); [[/gate]]task_prompt {prompt_name, prompt_arguments, profile_id} (Optimize profiles only — runs an MCP prompt); task_function {expression}; decision {condition}; [[gate:files]]file_input {file_id} (reads a file kept in Files — a table arrives as rows, a document as its text; get the id from TDA_Files 'list'); file_output {source, format: 'auto'|'csv'|'md'|'json'|'txt', filename} (keeps its input in Files on every run); [[/gate]]

node_updates.description: Fields to update on a node for 'update_node'.

edge.description: Edge definition for 'add_edge'. Fields: id (optional), source (node_id), target (node_id), type ('normal'|'error'|'conditional'|'cycle'), condition ('true'|'false' for conditional edges).

after_node_id.description: For 'insert_node': the node ID to insert after. The backend splices the new node into the existing outgoing edge automatically — no separate add_edge calls needed.

scope.description: Loop definition for 'create_scope'. Fields: name, node_ids (steps that follow one another — a round starts at one step and ends at one), max_iterations (int 1–20, default 3), optional history_window (earlier rounds each step sees) and exit_when ({node: a Judge in the loop, mode: 'pass'}). The back edge is added for you.

scope_updates.description: Fields to update on a loop for 'update_scope': name, max_iterations (1–20), history_window (int or null = all rounds), exit_when ({node, mode:'pass'} | {node, mode:'threshold', threshold} | {node, mode:'expression', expression} | null). Members cannot be changed in place.

input_params.description: Runtime parameter overrides for 'execute'. Merged with flow's global_params.

global_params.description: Flow-level variables accessible to all nodes. For 'create' or 'update'.

topology.description: For 'create': start from a topology template — 'pipeline' | 'parallel' | 'fork-join' | 'conditional' | 'iterative' (one agent refines until a judge passes it; slots: worker) | 'debate' (debaters argue in rounds until a moderator calls consensus, then a synthesiser writes it up; slots: debater, synthesiser) | 'teacher-student' (slots: student, teacher — the teacher decides when the student passes) | 'pair-programming' (driver writes code into a canvas, navigator approves; slots: driver, navigator). Judge/moderator slots default to the eval judge panel. The skeleton's agent slots are then filled with 'fills' or later via update_node. Omit for a blank flow.

params.description: For 'create' with a topology: its parameters, e.g. {stages: 3} (pipeline), {tasks: 3} (parallel), {branches: 3} (fork-join / conditional), {max_rounds: 3} (iterative / teacher-student / pair-programming), {debaters: 3, max_rounds: 3} (debate). Values are clamped to each template's range.

fills.description: For 'create' with a topology: which agent fills which slot — keyed by slot ROLE with a list in slot order (e.g. {stage: ['@A','@B','@C']}) or a single @TAG for every slot of that role (e.g. {synthesiser: '@S'}), or by slot node_id. An unknown @TAG is rejected, never written.

intensity_tooltips.medium: Use TDA_Flow when user explicitly asks about creating or running a workflow
intensity_tooltips.heavy: Proactively suggest flows for multi-step, recurring, or complex tasks
